chunks.content: ## Introduction to Adding an Inner Waist Drawstring in CLO This section explains the process of adding an inner waist drawstring to pants using CLO software, focusing on key tools such as the 2D and 3D windows, positioning ball tool, fixing needle, and simulation features. It outlines how to position, sew, and simulate the drawstring for a natural fit. ## Selecting and Positioning the Drawstring Material Begin by opening the material library in the left window of CLO. Navigate to the "drawstring" folder and select the first drawstring material file. Add it to the workspace by right-clicking. Use the positioning ball tool to move and rotate the drawstring closer to the hole on the inner waist panel where it will be inserted. To facilitate positioning without interference, reactivate the virtual model and hide the right click menu, then freeze the pants to prevent unwanted movement during adjustments. ## Sewing the Drawstring to the Inner Waist Panel In the 2D window, align the drawstring panel with the inner waist panel based on the marked sewing lines. It is crucial to avoid reversing the panels when sewing to ensure proper attachment. Use the fixing needle tool to temporarily fix the upper part of the drawstring before closing the sewing. This step helps maintain alignment and prevents shifting during simulation. ## Adjusting Drawstring Position and Simulation in 3D Switch to the 3D window and use the positioning ball tool again to fine-tune the drawstring’s placement near the hole, ensuring it naturally enters and exits the waist. After positioning, press Ctrl+W to remove the fixing needles, then activate the simulation mode by pressing the Control key. Allow the simulation to run until the drawstring and pants stabilize, which may take some time depending on the system performance. ## Refining Drawstring Appearance and Behavior After the initial simulation, review the drawstring’s fit and natural fall, especially at the corners where it may appear unnatural. The small particle diameter of the drawstring can cause stiffness; adjust this setting to a diameter of 1 to improve flexibility. Remodel the drawstring after adjusting particle size to achieve a more realistic drape. ## Finalizing Material and Color Adjustments Once the physical simulation and modeling are satisfactory, customize the drawstring and hook parts by changing their material properties and colors to match the desired design. Remove any temporary holes in the drawstring plate and run a final simulation to ensure overall stability and appearance. ## Completion The inner waist drawstring with hook-and-loop fastening is now fully integrated, simulating a natural outward appearance through the hole in the pants’ waistline. This method enhances garment realism and functionality within CLO.
